post.caption: Sphene is named for a wedge. Its crystals often grow as flat wedges, and many are twinned. French mineralogist Rene Just Hauy chose the name in 1801. Its other name, titanite, refers to the titanium it contains. Since 1982, mineralogists officially say titanite, yet jewelers still say sphene. Fire is how a gem splits white light into colored flashes. Sphene's fire measures 0.051, while diamond's measures 0.044. Turn a sphene and it shows three different colors. It is soft, only 5 to 5.5 on the Mohs scale. Chrome sphene is the intense green kind, colored by chromium.
